results.raw_hits_note: Approximate count of reqs touched at board level across the 3 parallel collection forks, summed from each fork's reported per-source req counts (Datadog 387, Elastic 385, Grafana Labs 139, Canonical 318, Cloudflare 504, Stripe 778, Okta 374, Zscaler 388, GitLab 246, Reddit 149, Tenable 49, Fastly 48, Palantir 306, Crusoe 316, Hut8 47, Sunrun ~251, ChargePoint 42, Leidos multi-sweep ~316, DigitalOcean 132, Chainguard 110, Epic Games 139, Bugcrowd 11, Netlify 6, Stacklok 2, plus Garner Health/SmarterDx/Coalfire/TENEX.AI/DigiCert/Corelight and many smaller boards). This undercounts true scan volume since not every individual JD within large boards was opened — only keyword/title-matched candidates were read in full.
results.collection_method_note: Three collection forks ran in parallel, each scoped to a disjoint slice of resources/sources.md: (1) cloud-native tech + Seattle-area majors, (2) energy-sector + Palantir/Leidos, (3) newly-formalized/promising-leads/aggregators + a fresh discovery sweep for brand-new sources. Each fork performed its own Step 3.5 live-URL validation inline (ATS JSON API primary, WebFetch fallback) and did not write any files or commit. The orchestrating main thread compiled all 3 forks' qualifying roles (24 total, no cross-fork duplicates this run), curated to 15 for quality/redundancy, wrote the report/log, updated resources/sources.md, attempted the dashboard update, and committed.

token_usage.note: Exact figures for all 3 collection forks, taken directly from their completion notifications. Main-thread usage is not measurable precisely; proxy below.

main_thread_tool_calls_estimate.note: Main thread (orchestrator) made 0 direct curl/API calls this run -- all collection/filtering/Step-3.5 validation was performed by the 3 forks above. Main thread read sources.md/workflow/prior logs, compiled/curated 24 qualifying roles down to 15, wrote the report/log, edited resources/sources.md, and handled the dashboard update and commit.

timing.note: step2 wall-clock time approximated from the longest-running fork's duration_ms (~574s); the 3 forks ran concurrently rather than sequentially, so this is far less than the sum of their individual durations (~21 min serial equivalent).
